operations.name: Saw Cut Gear Blanks
operations.setup_note: Cut individual blanks from round bar with sufficient axial stock for facing both sides. Segregate blanks by heat and material batch.

operations.name: CNC Turn – First Blank Setup
operations.setup_note: Grip the sawn blank in chuck jaws, face the first side, and machine the blank OD before opening the central bore. Establish a provisional datum A axis while leaving controlled stock on the bore and face for post-heat-treatment hard turning.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Second Blank Setup
operations.setup_note: Reverse the soft blank into bored soft jaws located from the machined OD and provisional datum axis. Face the second side parallel to the first and form the opposite bore-entry chamfer while retaining hard-turn stock on both faces.

operations.name: Finish Blank Inspection Gate
operations.setup_note: Locate the soft blank from its bore and face. Verify blank OD, bore size, face flatness, parallelism, and machining allowance before releasing it to tooth generation.

operations.name: Helical Gear Hobbing
operations.setup_note: Mount the inspected blank on a bore-locating arbor with axial face support. Generate the 61-tooth left-hand helical form relative to the provisional datum A axis, leaving the prescribed shaving stock.

operations.name: Soft Gear Shaving
operations.setup_note: Locate the hobbed gear from its bore and reference face. Shave the unhardened tooth flanks to achieve the DIN quality 8 profile, lead, pitch, and surface condition before heat treatment.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Deburr
operations.setup_note: Support the shaved gear on a clean bench fixture. Remove hobbing and shaving burrs from tooth ends, roots, bore entries, and blank edges without performing the required final post-heat-treatment tooth chamfer.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Inspection Gate
operations.setup_note: Inspect the shaved and deburred gear from datum A. Verify span measurement, profile, lead, pitch, blank OD, and bore condition before furnace release.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Washing
operations.setup_note: Wash and fully dry the accepted gears before furnace loading. Remove cutting oil, coolant, loose abrasive, marker residue, and fingerprints from all exposed surfaces.

operations.name: Case Harden, Quench and Temper
operations.setup_note: Rack the gears with separation and axial support for uniform atmosphere exposure and distortion control; the 100-piece order may be treated as one batch if validated furnace loading permits. Carburize, quench, and temper to the drawing hardness and effective case-depth requirements.

operations.name: Post-Heat-Treatment Teeth Chamfering
operations.setup_note: Locate the hardened gear in a bore-and-pitch-indexing fixture on the 5-axis VMC dedicated to this operation. Chamfer the hardened tooth end faces and tip edges before blasting, without recutting the tooth flanks.

operations.name: Post-Heat-Treatment Shot Blast
operations.setup_note: Blast the chamfered hardened gears using controlled media and exposure. Remove heat-treatment scale and residual burrs without damaging the tooth profile or consuming the remaining hard-turn allowance.

operations.name: Heat-Treatment Verification
operations.setup_note: Inspect blasted gears and the associated witness coupon before hard machining. Verify surface hardness, effective case depth certification, and unacceptable heat-treatment distortion.

operations.name: CNC Hard Turn – Bore and Faces
operations.setup_note: Locate the hardened gear from its tooth pitch geometry in a qualified narrow-contact fixture with opposed-access tooling. Hard turn the bore to establish final datum A, then finish both faces and bore entries in the same qualified operation while preserving tooth-to-bore runout.

operations.name: Post-Hard-Turning Washing
operations.setup_note: Wash the hard-turned gears as a standalone operation. Remove cutting oil, CBN swarf, loose chips, and residue from the finished bore, faces, and teeth before final measurement.

operations.name: Final Dimensional and Gear Inspection
operations.setup_note: Thermally stabilize and inspect the clean finished gear from final datum A. Verify the Ø15 H7 bore, face width, OD-to-bore runout, tooth span, profile, lead, pitch, and DIN 58405 quality requirements.

operations.name: Final Edge and Burr Verification
operations.setup_note: Handle the accepted gear on a protected bench and verify that no loose burrs or hazardous sharp edges remain after inspection. Perform only non-cutting hand cleanup that does not alter the H7 bore, tooth geometry, or controlled runout surfaces.

clarifications.question: What tooth-tip rounding value is required for parameter r_k?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the standard DIN 3972 profile II tool geometry with no special tooth-tip rounding beyond the specified edge-break requirement.

clarifications.question: Which specific surfaces are assigned the bracketed Rz 6 and Rz 2.5 finish requirements?
clarifications.suggested_default: Apply general Rz 25 unless a feature-specific leader is confirmed; provisionally apply Rz 6 to the H7 bore and do not apply Rz 2.5 without a confirmed leader.

clarifications.question: Is a dedicated setup on the listed 5-axis VMC acceptable for the required post-heat-treatment tooth chamfering operation?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the VMC 5-axis as a separate indexed hard-chamfering operation because no dedicated teeth-chamfer machine family is listed in the shop inventory.

assumptions.text: At 100 pieces, machining from round bar is preferred over developing a forging process; provisional 68 mm diameter by 16 mm blanks follow the stated bar-stock allowance guidance.
The stock weight is estimated from the provisional blank dimensions using nominal steel density; purchasing weight may vary with actual bar tolerance and saw kerf.
The soft-machined bore and both faces retain controlled stock for the corrected post-heat-treatment CNC hard-turning operation rather than being accepted at final size before carburizing.
Per GEAR-002, post-heat-treatment ID grinding, bore honing, face grinding, and OD grinding are removed and replaced by one CNC hard-turning operation covering the bore and both faces.
Per GEAR-001, gear grinding and teeth honing are omitted because DIN quality 8 is achieved by soft hobbing followed by shaving.

Turning-template grooving, threading, and part-off steps are omitted because no grooves or threads exist and individually sawn blanks are used; hole-making pilot drilling, peck drilling, reaming, tapping, and counterboring are omitted because they are not required by the short central through-bore.
The bore-finishing template's post-hardening grinding, honing, and lapping stages are superseded by the authoritative hard-turning correction; final bore verification remains in final inspection.

No coating is specified, so the plating/coating sequence, masking, curing, unmasking, and coating inspection are omitted; post-heat-treatment shot blasting is retained solely for scale and burr removal.

Heat-treatment masking, straightening, and separate stress relief are omitted because no selectively soft areas are specified and the part is a short disc rather than a slender shaft; furnace loading, cleaning, quenching, tempering, descaling, and hardness verification remain included.

The single corrected hard-turning operation assumes qualified tooth-pitch workholding and opposed-access tooling can finish the through-bore and both faces without losing the established tooth-to-bore relationship.
